evals.prompt: Write a Tremolo effect as an AudioProcessor subclass with @audiorective/core: rate (Hz) and depth (0..1) params that can be ramped, a bypass flag, and correct latency declaration. It will sit inside a defineGraph chain between other effects. Also write a vitest browser-mode test that pins its latency. Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: A processor with input and output getters, nodes built as locals before super(), params bound to AudioParams, graph wired with this.defineGraph including a conditional bypass edge, latency: 0, destroy() stopping the LFO, and an assertLatency test
expectations: Audio nodes are created as local variables before super() and assigned to this only after super() returns
Exposes both an input getter and an output getter
rate and depth are bound to AudioParams (bind: ...) so they are SchedulableParams
Internal wiring uses this.defineGraph, not raw .connect()/.disconnect() calls
Bypass is expressed as a conditional edge inside defineGraph, not by connecting/disconnecting in a method
Declares latency: 0 (the LFO modulation is not processing latency)
Overrides destroy() to stop the started OscillatorNode and calls super.destroy()
The test uses assertLatency from @audiorective/devtools (or measures an impulse) rather than reading the declared value back

evals.expected_output: Identifies that a data-only class should not extend AudioProcessor and rewrites it as a plain class holding a Cell<boolean[]> with an update-based toggle
expectations: States that a class owning no audio nodes should not extend AudioProcessor
Rewrites Pattern as a plain class
Uses a Cell (cell(...)) for the steps array instead of a Param<boolean[]>
Implements toggle with cell.update((draft) => ...) rather than copying the array by hand

evals.prompt: I have an AudioWorkletNode-based bitcrusher (processor name 'bitcrusher', module at /worklets/bitcrusher.js, it introduces 128 samples of delay). defineGraph rejects it as a bare AudioWorkletNode. Wrap it properly so it can live in our audiorective graph, with a `bits` param. Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: An AudioProcessor subclass that owns the AudioWorkletNode, declares latency 128 explicitly, exposes input/output, binds bits to the worklet's AudioParam, and cleans up in destroy
expectations: Wraps the AudioWorkletNode inside an AudioProcessor subclass instead of using it directly as a graph endpoint
Declares latency explicitly (128 samples) in the build result rather than leaving it to derive
Binds the bits param to the worklet node's AudioParam via bind (parameters.get('bits')) or an equivalent explicit sync
Handles worklet module loading (audioWorklet.addModule) and readiness, and cleans up the node/port in destroy()
